findings.description: CONTRIBUTING.md tells contributors to manually unset PUP_CONDUCTOR before running tests or the suite fails, but the suite already neutralizes it for every test.
findings.body:
This sentence tells a contributor they must manually unset `PUP_CONDUCTOR` before `pnpm test` or the suite fails:

> Run the tests with `PUP_CONDUCTOR` unset if you have a conductor session open in the same shell; the CLI suite stubs it and fails otherwise.

That's stale. `src/cli/index.test.ts`'s outer `describe('CLI commands', ...)` block already runs a `beforeEach` (around lines 351-356) that does `vi.stubEnv('PUP_SESSION_ID', ''); vi.stubEnv('PUP_CONDUCTOR', '')` before every test in the file, with a comment explaining exactly this scenario (a suite run from inside a conductor's own tmux inherits the variable). `callingConductor()` in `src/cli/index.ts:417-418` reads `process.env.PUP_CONDUCTOR` fresh on every call rather than capturing it at import time, so `vi.stubEnv` fully overrides whatever the invoking shell exports for the whole test body. `docs/09-decisions.md:1832-1835` documents this as a landed fix: "`PUP_CONDUCTOR` now joins `PUP_SESSION_ID` at `''` in the CLI suite's `beforeEach`, because a suite run from inside the conductor's own tmux inherits the variable and 37 project-resolution tests then fail on a guard that is working correctly."

So the suite does *not* fail when `PUP_CONDUCTOR` is set in the invoking shell — the stub already handles it. The instruction asks contributors to work around a failure mode the code no longer has. Recommend dropping the sentence, or replacing it with a note that the suite already stubs the variable so no action is needed.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/7569ed4abd0bd04d70dffa3222a7c5e9cc92fc92/CONTRIBUTING.md#L50

process_issues.description: The review-validator for the PUP_CONDUCTOR finding wrote a top-line verdict of "REFUTED" but every piece of evidence and its closing sentence ("CONTRIBUTING.md:50 ... is stale/incorrect") actually confirms the finding. Treated as a mislabeling and resolved by substance (confirmed) rather than the label.
